Status.note: EKPC told the Kentucky Public Service Commission on March 20, 2026 that site clearing would begin March 23, 2026, the groundbreaking would be May 20, 2026 and construction would start June 1, 2026. The June 2026 semi-annual report lists Construction Start as June 2026 at 0 percent and says the final air permit of March 6, 2026 pulled the schedule up. I did not find a dated report that work was actually under way. So the current status of construction is kept, but this is a single owner source and rests on planned dates. The press release of May 20, 2026 from EKPC, read as a saved copy at https://web.archive.org/web/20260614220816/https://www.ekpc.coop/sites/default/files/PDFs/2026/2026-05-20__EKPC_breaks_ground_on_Liberty_Station.pdf, says the same: construction is expected to begin in June 2026 and the plant should operate in late 2028.

qa.question: Should Liberty Station stay at construction when EIA lists it as planned?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists all 12 engines as planned with regulatory approvals not initiated, though the commission certificate was granted May 20, 2025 and the air permit was issued March 6, 2026. EKPC's own filings give planned dates for site work and a May 20, 2026 groundbreaking, and the June 2026 report shows construction start at 0 percent.
qa.recommendation: Leave the status as construction. Check EKPC's next semi-annual report, due about December 2026, for the actual construction start.
qa.note: I found a May 2026 press report of the groundbreaking at https://marcellusdrilling.com/?p=119142 and a trade piece at https://www.electric.coop/ekpcs-new-gas-plant-shows-strong-investment-in-rural-kentucky-community but no independent dated report of work under way. EIA is likely just behind the permits.

qa.question: When did Liberty Station reach the construction step?
qa.finding: EKPC's letter of March 20, 2026 at https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2024-00310/greg.cecil@ekpc.coop/03202026030536/Closed/Letter_Liberty_RICE__construction_commencement.pdf planned tree clearing from March 23, 2026, a groundbreaking on May 20, 2026 and construction from June 1, 2026. The report at https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2024-00310/greg.cecil@ekpc.coop/06052026074625/Closed/PSC_semi-annual_Report_June_2026_-_Liberty_RICE.pdf lists construction start as June 2026 and not yet done as of the reporting period ending May 2026.
qa.recommendation: Date the construction step June 2026, the month EKPC says construction begins in its press release at https://web.archive.org/web/20260614220816/https://www.ekpc.coop/sites/default/files/PDFs/2026/2026-05-20__EKPC_breaks_ground_on_Liberty_Station.pdf and its June 2026 report to the commission. Update the date if a later EKPC report gives an earlier or later actual start.
qa.note: I read the commission docket for case 2024-00310, EKPC's construction page at https://www.ekpc.coop/liberty-station-construction, the press release of May 20, 2026 as a saved copy, and press coverage. All give planned dates. None says work actually began.

qa.question: Should Backup Power stay no for Liberty Station?
qa.finding: The application describes a dual fuel peaking facility that sells to the grid, with diesel as an alternate fuel. No document calls the engines backup for another site.
qa.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no. Backup Power applies to data center sites, and none was found here.
qa.note: Searched the application at https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2024-00310/allyson%40hloky.com/09202024100053/Application_with_Exhibits.pdf and the air permit. Nothing states the value either way. The air permit lists an emergency generator and a fire pump engine, but these support the plant itself and are not generating units sold to the grid.

qa.question: Does EKPC's 2025 plan list a different size for Liberty Station?
qa.finding: The US IRPs tab note says the plan lists 214 MW of engines at Liberty Station, which matches the net figure in the commission order and not GEM's 217.2 MW nameplate.
qa.recommendation: Leave capacity at 217.2 MW and add the plan to the IRP Notes line.
qa.note: I did not open the plan PDF itself, so no finding is marked as from the plan.
